division_name: The Adventure Of The Noble Bachelor

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective living in Baker Street; narrator Watson's friend; takes Lord St. Simon's case and solves it.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion and fellow lodger in Baker Street; a doctor back from Afghanistan with a wounded leg.

characters.name: Lord Robert St. Simon
characters.note: Aristocratic second son of the Duke of Balmoral, around forty-one, pale and fussy, who married Hatty Doran and was deserted at the wedding breakfast.

characters.name: Hatty Doran
characters.note: Daughter of Aloysius Doran of San Francisco; the bride who vanished at the wedding breakfast to run off with her first husband Frank Moulton.

characters.name: Francis Hay Moulton
characters.note: Small, wiry, sunburnt American prospector, Hatty's first husband, presumed dead in the Apache attack; appears as the man in the pew at the wedding.

characters.name: Lestrade
characters.note: Inspector of Scotland Yard working the case; wears a pea-jacket and drags the Serpentine.

characters.name: Flora Millar
aliases: the woman who caused the disturbance
characters.note: Former dancer at the Allegro and former mistress of Lord St. Simon; arrested after causing a disturbance at the Doran house. Not to be confused with Frank Moulton, whose initials are also F. H. M.

characters.name: Alice
characters.note: Hatty Doran's American maid from California, who packed the bride's ulster and bonnet.

characters.name: Aloysius Doran
characters.note: Rich San Francisco mining man and father of Hatty Doran.

characters.name: Duke of Balmoral
characters.note: Father of Lord St. Simon; referred to but absent from the action.

characters.name: Lord Backwater
characters.note: Acquaintance who recommended Holmes to Lord St. Simon; referred to but absent.

locations.name: Baker Street rooms
locations.note: Holmes and Watson's shared lodgings, where the interviews and supper take place.

locations.name: Grosvenor Mansions
locations.note: Lord St. Simon's residence, named in his letter; referred to only.

locations.name: St. George's, Hanover Square
locations.note: Church where the wedding ceremony took place.

locations.name: Doran house, Lancaster Gate
locations.note: Furnished house at Lancaster Gate where the wedding breakfast took place and the bride vanished.

locations.name: Hyde Park
locations.note: Park into which Hatty followed Frank after leaving the house.

locations.name: the Serpentine
locations.note: Lake in Hyde Park where Lestrade dragged for the bride's body and found her wedding clothes.

locations.name: Gordon Square
locations.note: Lodgings where Hatty and Frank went after leaving the Park.

brief.tone: Urbane Victorian detective mystery with a wry, faintly comic undertone and domestic intimacy in the Baker Street rooms.
depiction_rules: Show Holmes and Watson in the Baker Street rooms in Victorian dress, with fire, papers, and the supper laid out.
Lord St. Simon is a fastidious aristocrat: high collar, frock-coat, yellow gloves, golden eyeglasses on a cord.
Hatty Doran should be shown with lustrous dark hair and a striking face, consistent with the ivory miniature.
Do not show the bride's flight or the Serpentine search as violent; keep the mood civil and sly.
Avoid depicting the Apache attack in detail; Frank's past is told only in speech.

era.name: Victorian London, c. 1888-1890s, with American Western backstory (California, Montana, Arizona, New Mexico)
era.people: English aristocrats, Scotland Yard officers, and London servants; Americans from San Francisco and mining camps of the Rockies and the Pacific slope, rugged and sunburnt.
era.dress: Frock-coats, high collars, top hats, ulsters and bonnets for women, wedding silk and satin with veil and wreath; policemen in pea-jacket and cravat for Lestrade.
era.buildings_and_objects: Gas-lit Baker Street lodgings with mahogany table and basket-chair, Hanover Square church, Lancaster Gate townhouse, Hyde Park and the Serpentine, Northumberland Avenue hotel, cards, newspapers, and cigars.
era.technology: Newspapers and printed society columns, hansom cabs, handwritten letters with quill pens, pencil notes; no telephone or photography beyond the miniature and cartes.
